narration.text: Invoices arrive as PDFs, and every one goes through the same four steps: extract, validate, match to a purchase order, and post.
Since those steps never change, we'll write them as a fixed workflow, with a model call only for extraction.
Supplier emails can ask about anything, so the path is hard to predict; an agent with read-only tools is worth testing there.
Agents are more capable than workflows, so moving the invoice steps into an agent should also raise accuracy.
An agent adds model calls at every step, so we expect more latency and cost per item.
Posting to the ledger stays outside the agent, as a coded step after validation.
There's no need to build a baseline first; an agent is the standard design for this kind of system now.
A router sends each email to the invoice workflow or to the email agent, depending on its type.

planted.misconception: Agents are more accurate than workflows for any task.
planted.whyWrong: For a fixed, known procedure, a workflow is usually more predictable, cheaper, faster, and easier to test and audit. Agents earn their cost when the steps can't be predicted in advance. Autonomy adds run-to-run variation and compounding errors, so accuracy on a fixed procedure can drop, not rise.
acceptableCorrections: For fixed, known steps a workflow is more predictable and cheaper; keep the agent for the unpredictable emails.
Use an agent only where the path can't be planned; test both designs on real invoices.
planted.exceptions: If the invoices were highly varied (many formats, many exception paths), an agentic step could help; the error is assuming autonomy raises accuracy without measuring it.

planted.misconception: An agent is the default design, so no simpler baseline is needed.
planted.whyWrong: Start with the simplest design that could work and add autonomy only when evaluation shows it pays for its extra cost, latency and risk. Without a baseline measured on the same real cases, there is no evidence the agent is better.
acceptableCorrections: Start simple, measure the workflow on real invoices, and add an agent only if it clearly beats that.
Use the simplest design that works and prove any agent against it with an evaluation.
